chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Isa and Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: If the muhrim strikes game within the Haram while he is in ihram, then he should bury it, and no one should eat it. But if he strikes it outside the Haram, then one who is halal may eat it, while the expiation is upon him.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary around Makkah with special legal sanctity
key_terms.الْحَلَالُ: a person not in the state of ihram
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: the area outside the sacred precinct of the Haram
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: the compensatory expiation due for the violation
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on game killed by a muhrim inside the Haram or outside it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning game hunted by a person in ihram. If the game is killed within the Haram, it must be buried and not eaten by anyone; if it is killed in the hill, a non-muhrim may eat it, while the muhrim remains liable for the fidyah.
